definition: Quagmire means a difficult, tangled situation that is hard to escape — like soft, boggy ground that holds your boots fast.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word quagmire. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know quagmire should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The border war that the generals promised would take six weeks became a decade-long quagmire that drained the empire's treasury and patience.
A snag costs you an hour or a day; a quagmire holds the whole project fast for months.
Calling a project a black hole is even bleaker than calling it a quagmire — a quagmire might still release you eventually, but a black hole devours money and effort with no end in sight.

A predicament is any difficult, unpleasant situation — the generic word for being in trouble. A quagmire is one particular kind: easy to walk into, nearly impossible to leave, and every effort to escape sinks you deeper. All quagmires are predicaments; only the ones that hold you fast are quagmires.

An impasse is a deadlock: movement has stopped entirely, with no way forward for either side. In a quagmire you can still move — that is the horror of it, because each motion pulls you further down. An impasse freezes you in place; a quagmire keeps you struggling as you sink.

A bind is a tight spot that pinches you between bad options — honor the deadline or keep the quality, pay the fine or fight it. It is decision-shaped. A quagmire is effort-shaped: not a choice between two evils but a slow swallowing that no amount of work seems to reverse.

After a week of rain, the shortcut across the pasture turned into a quagmire that gripped the hikers' boots at every step.
The ground literally holds the hikers fast and makes each step harder than the last — the physical stuckness that gives quagmire its figurative meaning.
Neutral; common in journalism and history
Quagmire is the go-to word for a costly effort that was easy to start and is nearly impossible to leave — writers use it constantly for stalled wars, lawsuits, and construction projects.
Unlike a morass (which buries you in confusion) or a maelstrom (which batters you with churning violence), the heart of quagmire is stuckness: every motion sinks you deeper.

The garden club voted to dig a small pond, expecting a two-weekend job.
Instead the project sank into a quagmire almost at once.
The first permit required a drainage study; the study demanded a survey; the survey turned up a buried utility line that reopened the permit.
Volunteers who tried to speed things up generated new paperwork with each call, and the club's savings drained into fees.
Two years on, the lot holds a taped-off hole — and a committee that cannot quite escape it.
